Labs Designer & Facilitator – UK/Ireland

24-32 hours per week

Location: Remote from the UK or Ireland

Maternity cover until September 2027, with possibility of extension

Preferred starting date: December 2026

Are you passionate about designing and facilitating participatory processes that drive systemic change for holistic landscape restoration? Do you thrive in complex, multi-stakeholder environments and enjoy working with grassroots movements to co-create regenerative futures? Then this might be the role for you!

Commonland supports a growing network of landscape restoration initiatives across the UK and Ireland. Through long-term, collaborative learning journeys (Labs) we aim to strengthen leadership, build a learning and action community, and address systemic barriers to holistic restoration. These labs go beyond one-off workshops - they are multi-year, collaborative processes that move from shared understanding to experimentation and action, helping communities tackle root causes of degradation and build regenerative landscapes. The UK/Ireland Lab is currently being co-designed with landscape partners. You will step into co-responsibility for its continued design and delivery. 

The role is positioned within Commonland's international Learning Team and is part of the wider Landscape Development and Support Team. For the Lab specifically, you will work closely with the UK/Ireland Team. 

What You'll Do

  • Lead the co-design and delivery of the UK/Ireland Lab, building from a structured handover and adapting the programme to the UK and Irish context while maintaining alignment with Commonland's strategy
  • Develop participatory, multi-stakeholder learning processes using systems thinking, design methodologies, and transformative facilitation
  • Support landscape partners in identifying and addressing root causes of environmental and social challenges, including structural barriers and power dynamics
  • Strengthen connections among participating landscape initiatives as a learning community and action-oriented partnership
  • Collaborate with and support a small pool of facilitators and hosts to deliver impactful learning experiences

Globally focused:

  • Contribute to Commonland's global learning infrastructure and share insights across regions, including a global Lab Designers community of practice and an organisation-wide Commonland global team retreat
  • Support the development of tools and guides that serve landscape partners and Labs globally, including learning infrastructure, the Landscape Governance Canvas, and the Landscape System Mapping Toolkit currently in development

What You Bring

You are someone who:

  • Strategic mindset – You see ahead to future possibilities and translating them into breakthrough strategies.
  • Communicates effectively – You develop and deliver multimode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences. 
  • Manages ambiguity – You operate effectively and can experiment, adapt and learn even when things are not certain, or the way forward is not clear.
  • Collaborates – You build partnerships and working collaboratively with others to meet shared objectives and deliver stakeholder-centric solutions.
  • Builds networks – You effectively build formal and informal learning networks inside and outside the organisation.
  • Project management – You initiate, plan, execute, and monitor initiatives efficiently, balancing scope, resources, timelines, and risks to deliver measurable outcomes. 

You also bring:

  • Experience in participatory process design, facilitation, and working with diverse stakeholder groups
  • The ability to lead and guide a programme design and hosting team 
  • A good understanding of the UK and/or Irish landscape restoration, environmental, or grassroots context; direct professional experience in this field and geography is highly valuable
  • Based in the UK or Ireland, legally eligible to work there, and able to travel regularly across the region
  • Fluency in English

What We Offer

  • A purpose-driven role where your work contributes directly to restoring landscapes and shaping a regenerative future
  • Flexibility to work remotely, with the freedom to design your workday in a way that suits your life and energy
  • A supportive team culture with room to grow, with opportunities for personal and professional development through learning, reflection, and experimentation
  • A consultancy agreement including a market-conform salary

How to Apply

We are excited to learn more about you and how your competencies fit this role. Please submit your CV via the application link before 5 October 2026 and answer a few questions related to the key criteria for this position. Your responses will help us assess all candidates fairly and consistently.

Landscape Developer – UK & Ireland

32-40 hours per week 

Location: Remote within UK/Ireland

One-year contract with possibility of extension 

Preferred starting date: 1 December 2026

Are you passionate about driving systemic change in landscape restoration through strategic partnerships, finance and fundraising, and collaborative learning? Do you thrive in complex, multi-stakeholder environments and enjoy bridging gaps between funders, governments, and grassroots initiatives? This could be the role for you.

Commonland supports a growing network of landscape scale restoration initiatives across the UK and Ireland. Through long-term, collaborative Learning and Social Lab networks, we aim to strengthen leadership, enhance enabling conditions, and address systemic barriers to holistic landscape restoration and regeneration. This goes beyond one-off workshops: we are working together with our partners to consciously develop multi-year, systemic multistakeholder processes that move from building shared understanding, to experimentation and action, helping key actors tackle root causes of degradation and build regenerative landscapes.

Your impact

  • Support landscape partners across the UK & Ireland with direct strategic support and connect with system-level actors (companies, funders, government bodies, foundations, and knowledge institutions)
  • Secure funding and financing mechanisms by unlocking Ireland’s incoming nature restoration law funding and engaging the UK nature finance & funding landscape, and matchmaking between finance providers and landscape partners.
  • Co-design innovative responses to systemic barriers to- and opportunities for holistic landscape restoration, leveraging existing relationships to bring about systemic changes.
  • Co-develop a comprehensive fundraising strategy, identifying and mapping UK, Irish, and European public/private funding opportunities.
  • Support landscape partners in developing systemic innovations (e.g., bioregional finance, payment for ecosystem services, learning networks) and scaling credible alternatives to current economic models.
  • Organise learning sessions to build partners’ fundraising and facilitation capacity, aligning with the regions evolving social innovation lab structure.
  • Collaborate with Commonland’s global learning community to share insights and ensure strategic alignment with the European Landscape restoration community.

This role includes regular travel within the UK and Ireland, with occasional international travel.

What You Bring

You are someone who:

  • Designs partnerships, programmes and processes: You build processes grounded in ambition to create long-term, holistic and regenerative system change, balancing structure with adaptability.
  • Thinks in systems: Connect themes (e.g., upland dynamics, agri-food innovation), can sit with the discomfort of complexity, and intentionally and attentionally guide others through change.
  • Communicates with empathy and understanding: You listen deeply, build trust across diverse stakeholders, and foster inclusive collaboration with stakeholders.
  • Operates from shared purpose: You connect people, ideas, and interests to unlock collective potential.
  • Learns and adapts: You’re open-minded, curious, and quick to adjust to emerging needs and insights while maintaining the momentum.
  • Results-driven: You combine innovative thinking with structured execution to deliver tangible outcomes.

You also bring

  • Several years experience in fundraising, partnership development, and/or landscape restoration, with a track record in the UK/Ireland.
  • Solid understanding of the UK/Ireland’s environmental, agricultural, or rural and sustainable development sectors.
  • Strong nature finance & funding literacy, including a clear view of where funding and market-based finance mechanisms deliver and where they don't, and interest in regenerative, new economy and bioregional approaches.
  • Fluency in English; additional bioregional languages (e.g., Welsh, Irish) are a plus.
  • A broad network of stakeholders working in landscape restoration in the UK/Ireland.

What We Offer

  • A purpose-driven role where your work directly contributes to restoring the conditions that create thriving landscapes and shaping a regenerative future.
  • A competitive gross monthly salary between €5,100 and €6,000 (based on 40 hours/week), tailored to your level of experience and local cost of living.
  • Flexibility to work remotely, with the freedom to design your workday to suit your life and energy, as well as work commitments and fixtures.
  • Room to grow, with opportunities for personal and professional development through learning, reflection, and experimentation including a personal learning budget of 1,750 GBP/ 2,000 euro per year.
  • A supportive team culture that values creativity, collaboration, and continuous learning.
